issues.description: Animal is specified to have only the attribute `name: String` (and constructors initializing all attributes accordingly), but the solution adds an additional attribute `age: int` in `Animal` and therefore requires all concrete animals (Seal/Pig/Goat) to be constructed with `(String name, int age)`. This contradicts the UML/spec and changes the required class model and constructor signatures for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the model consistent across spec/template/solution: either update the UML and text to include `age: int` and require `(name, age)` constructors everywhere, or remove `age` from `Animal` and from all subclass constructors to match the stated `name`-only model.

issues.description: The provided Main example constructs animals with a single-argument constructor (e.g., `new Seal("Clarabelle")`), but the solution classes only define constructors with two parameters `(String name, int age)`. If students follow the example, it will not compile against the provided solution/API expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the commented Main example to pass an age argument for each animal (and adjust any documentation accordingly), or add overloaded one-argument constructors (e.g., default age) to Seal/Pig/Goat (and/or Animal) so the example code compiles.
